ranked.headline: Inferring signaling and interaction networks from phosphoproteomic and proteomic data
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarking and time-resolved differential network models test whether inferred protein and kinase networks recover true structure.

ranked.headline: Fusing histology and spatial transcriptomics to refine single-cell tissue measurements
ranked.summary: Computational fusion of histology, spatial and single-cell data now corrects what each modality captures alone.

ranked.headline: Reusable software for multi-omics, spatial, single-cell and regulatory data analysis
ranked.summary: Recent tools package specialised omics analyses as interactive or scriptable software, lowering barriers to reuse across datasets.

ranked.headline: Learned representations tested for cross-setting transfer in biological prediction
ranked.summary: Cross-cohort and cross-modality generalization, rather than in-sample accuracy, is becoming the test for learned biological representations.

ranked.headline: Tools map RNA-protein binding, transcript quantification, and translational control
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and pipelines assess RNA-binding, transcript quantification, and translation methods on real and simulated data across species.

ranked.headline: Single-cell models encode lineage, barcode, and temporal structure to infer regulation
ranked.summary: Lineage barcodes, temporal diffusion models, and cis-regulatory profiles are now being built into single-cell regulation models, largely as preprints.

ranked.headline: Pangenome graphs resolve structural and transposable element variation across species
ranked.summary: Long-read assemblies and pangenome graphs now pair structural and transposable element variation with trait and adaptation associations.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic models link feedback structure to cross-scale biological dynamics
ranked.summary: Explicit feedback and constraint structure in mechanistic models now yields testable cross-scale dynamics across crop, organelle, and spike data.

ranked.headline: Long-read and targeted methods resolve DNA methylation and radiation-induced genomic…
ranked.summary: Long-read and targeted sequencing now resolve single-nucleotide methylation at defined loci and dose-time genome-integrity readouts.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks test whether computed conformational ensembles match experimental SAXS data
ranked.summary: Flexible multidomain proteins and intrinsically disordered regions demand ensemble models validated against experimental measurements rather than single static…

ranked.headline: Generative and latent-variable models for single-cell and spatial omics data
ranked.summary: Single-cell and spatial measurements carry dropout, batch effects and hidden factors that generative models now target directly.

ranked.headline: Pipelines recover sequence, taxa and transcripts from long-read and amplicon data
ranked.summary: Long-read and high-throughput sequencing tools are gaining speed, raw-signal handling, and UMI-aware error correction in recent 2026 preprints and publications.

ranked.headline: Bayesian and hierarchical inference methods for stochastic biological models and assays
ranked.summary: Recent tools model stochastic reaction dynamics, reporter-assay noise, and barcode fitness data with explicit probabilistic treatment of uncertainty.

ranked.headline: Computational models map sequence and chemistry into spaces for design and scoring
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply rule-based, language-model, and machine-learning pipelines to design or score molecular and organism-level outcomes.

ranked.headline: Language model and sequence-structure learning predict and design bioactive peptides
ranked.summary: Eight February 2026 records pair protein language model embeddings with generative and structure-aware models for peptide prediction and design.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and structure-aware models for omics and molecular property prediction
ranked.summary: Explicit phylogenetic and batch structure is now built into omics inference, alongside standardized benchmarks for chemistry and molecular prediction.

ranked.headline: Neural surrogates and diffusion models for molecular simulation and generation
ranked.summary: Learned models are now replacing or accelerating costly molecular simulation, sequencing, and generative design tasks across recent preprints and papers.

ranked.headline: Constraint and dual-coding regions extend variant prioritization beyond missense calls
ranked.summary: Recent work quantifies regional nonsense constraint across 730,947 individuals and maps splicing-derived dual-coding regions across the human genome.

ranked.headline: Software tools for selection scans, admixture, and read simulation in genomics
ranked.summary: Accelerated and automated genomic analysis tools are reducing the cost of selection scans, simulation, and phylogeographic inference.

ranked.headline: Multimodal and graph inputs address generalization limits in gene and RNA prediction
ranked.summary: Recent reports show longer sequences can hurt gene expression prediction, prompting explicit multimodal or graph-structured inputs.

ranked.headline: Sequence models predict enzyme function under limited labels and for unseen EC classes
ranked.summary: Limited annotation and unseen label spaces are pushing sequence-based models toward data-efficient and hierarchical prediction strategies.

ranked.headline: Synaptic tuning and connection type bound decodable and collective neural information
ranked.summary: Coarse synaptic tuning, energy-normalized coding efficiency, and Dale's-principle violations are now examined jointly as limits on neural coding.

ranked.headline: Graph and language models predict immune receptor-peptide recognition from structure and…
ranked.summary: Structure-aware graph and language models now target TCR, Ig, BCR and MHC-peptide binding, with generalization to unseen peptides under scrutiny.

ranked.headline: Generative and deep learning models prioritize molecules for experimental validation
ranked.summary: Generative and structure-aware models now feed directly into assay-validated lead prioritization across GPCR, TLR5, and Chrebp targets.

ranked.headline: Model-based methods extend genetic association inference beyond single-locus frameworks
ranked.summary: Large biobank and imaging datasets motivate association frameworks that go beyond conventional single-locus, fixed-reference designs.

ranked.headline: Repository-scale spectra and benchmarked pipelines widen peptide identification coverage
ranked.summary: Low-input DIA benchmarks, top-down spectral repositories, and immunopeptidogenomic pipelines are expanding peptide-level evidence recovery from MS data.

ranked.headline: Reaction network and surrogate models predict and steer gene expression behavior
ranked.summary: Explicit network and surrogate models are now used to predict and steer expression in cell-free, CRISPRa, and riboswitch systems.

ranked.headline: Protein language model embeddings guide mutant screening and CAR-T activity prediction
ranked.summary: PLM embeddings and fine-tuning are being tested as cheap sequence-only proxies for structural disruption and therapeutic cell activity.

ranked.headline: Graph and foundation models predict drug responses and cancer subtypes from omics data
ranked.summary: Knowledge graphs and single-cell foundation models are being paired to predict drug indications, perturbation responses, and synthetic lethality.

ranked.headline: Learned models of protein binding face scrutiny under perturbation and ligand class
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test whether AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2 hold up under sequence mutation and allosteric ligands, and release new binding datasets.

ranked.headline: Experimental observables benchmark RNA structure predictors and potentials
ranked.summary: Experimental observables such as FRET transfer efficiencies and Structure-seq data now arbitrate accuracy of RNA structure predictors and potentials.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomics maps complex, fold and accessory-genome architecture across lineages
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published archaeal study apply quantified comparative analysis to proteome and genome architecture across diverse lineages.

ranked.headline: Read-level tools assign taxa and resolve tandem repeat structure from sequencing data
ranked.summary: Mixed-sample and long-read sequencing data require read-level assignment to taxa and repeat arrays, tackled by alignment-based and alignment-free tools.

ranked.headline: Coarse-grained and geometric methods extended to absolute binding free energies
ranked.summary: Three recent preprints judge reduced-resolution and geometric methods quantitatively by absolute binding and folding free energies.

ranked.headline: Quantitative modeling links biomolecular structure to FRET readouts and dye properties
ranked.summary: Fresh work pairs FRET imaging, structural modeling and dye prediction to make fluorescence data quantitative for receptors and nanobody sensors.

ranked.headline: Graph-based methods are advancing spatial and single-cell omics analysis
ranked.summary: Spatial and paired single-cell multi-omic datasets demand graph-aware metrics that capture spatial organization beyond label agreement.

ranked.headline: Spatial omics methods link tumor protein and gene patterns to patient-level outcomes
ranked.summary: Multiplexed spatial profiling now supports segmentation-free and tumor-relative analyses of tissue organization in patient cohorts.

ranked.headline: Reduced equations and agent-based rules govern multicellular population dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair analytical reduction with simulation validation for tumor hypoxia, tuberculosis, demyelination and bacterial fixation.

ranked.headline: Network models rank drug repurposing and microbiome-modulated therapy candidates
ranked.summary: Graph-based and metabolic modeling of drug, microbial, and tumor networks now predict repurposing candidates and synergistic combinations.

ranked.headline: Models infer chromatin contacts and states from protein binding and epigenetic data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple protein binding profiles to predicted chromatin contact maps while correcting cohesin ChIP background bias at CTCF sites.
